text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Wednesday.

LONDON - British shares ended a choppy session mixed amid continued uncertainty about possible interest rate hikes, fears that rates could be tightened by both U.S. and UK central banks in the near-term kept many participants out of the market and capped a promising FTSE rally. The FTSE 100 index closed 0.7 of a point lower to 4,557.1.

FRANKFURT - German shares ended low-volume bourse trade one percent higher, market lacks impetus to forge more significant gains and continues to track late gains in electronic trade from Tuesday, weaker futures and debt impact on sentiment, effect of soothing words from both sides in gold revaluation row seen generally market-neutral. The DAX index ended at 3,661.84, up 36.10 points. In post-bourse trade the DAX index stood at 3,651.59.

PARIS - The Paris bourse finished in positive ground for the third straight session this week since the Socialists came to power, the market was enjoying a honeymoon period with the left and bargain hunting helped support prices. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 10.88 points or 0.41 percent to 2,635.37.

ZURICH - Shares posted a second straight record close, with the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) establishing itself firmly above the level of 5,200 that it hurdled on Tuesday. Prices came down slightly in late trade due to a weaker Wall Street start. "But let's not forget the SMI added more than 160 points in the past two sessions," one trader said. The SMI ended up 31.3 points, or 0.6 percent, at 5,238.5, while the all-share SPI was up 22.34 points, or 0.6 percent, to 3,313.71.

TOKYO - The Tokyo Nikkei index finished at a high for 1997 for the second consecutive day, as buying of high-tech laggards, semiconducter-related shares and some issues driven by domestic demand provided support. The 225-share Nikkei average ended 48.40 points or 0.24 percent higher at 20,611.56.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks finished modestly higher after profit-taking trimmed sharp early gains piled up during a blue-chip rebound led by property counters. The Hang Seng Index closed up 71.41 points or 0.48 percent to 14,831.58.

SYDNEY - The Australian stock market held a small gain all afternoon to the close, with little fresh news to drive a six-week rally to higher levels. The All Ordinaries Index pushed up about 10 points in late morning trade, but soon settled back to end the day 2.3 points higher at 2,615.9.

JOHANNESBURG - Still feasting on the surprisingly big leap in South Africa's May official reserves, Johannesburg shares powered ahead for the third consecutive day, hoisting the financial index to a fresh closing high, basket trading from futures arbitrage lifted heavyweight industrials but some massive gains in smaller stocks also aided the overall rise. The Industrial index ended up at 8,428.4, up 91.6 points, the All-share index up 60.8 to 7,172.8 and the Gold index was off 12.1 points to a fresh 50-month low of 1,145.7.
